title: The Catechism (1992)
hookLine: a single summary of Catholic belief, written for the whole world

lines: A LITTLE BOOK FOR EACH PLACE.
ONE BOOK FOR THE WHOLE CHURCH.
cards: If someone asked you what Catholics actually believe, where would you send them?
For a long time the answer depended on where you lived: each country, sometimes each diocese, had its own little question-and-answer book, and children memorized them. Who made us? God made us.
There had been a catechism for the whole Church once before, written after the Council of Trent for parish priests.

Then the bishops of the world, meeting in Rome, asked for a new one: one book for the whole Church, setting out the faith in order. It took years of drafting, and the bishops were asked for their comments.

teach.h: FOUR PARTS: BELIEVE, WORSHIP, LIVE, PRAY.
teach.b: Open it and the plan is plain. First, the shape: four parts, and once you know them the whole book opens up. The faith professed: the Creed, line by line.
The faith celebrated: the liturgy and the sacraments. The faith lived: the life in Christ, including the Ten Commandments. The faith prayed: prayer, ending with the Our Father, line by line.
Every paragraph is numbered, and the book cross-references itself in the margins, so a paragraph about baptism points you to others about grace, the Church, water at Easter.
People cite it by number, the way you'd cite a verse. Third, who it's for.

John Paul the Second, in the document that introduced it, called it a sure norm for teaching the faith, meant first for bishops and teachers, then for anyone who wants to know what the Church believes.
It was never meant to replace local catechisms, but to be the reference they draw on. Fourth, the sources.
Open it almost anywhere and the paragraphs are stitched from Scripture, the councils, saints and early writers.

teach.h: THAT THOU MAYEST KNOW THE VERITY.
teach.b: Luke opens his Gospel by telling Theophilus why he wrote it, in the Douay-Rheims: "That thou mayest know the verity of those words in which thou hast been instructed."
The Catechism sets out to do the same at the size of a whole Church: one summary, in order, so the faith can be known, not just guessed at.

how: Catholics use the Catechism of the Catholic Church as a reference in parish classes, adult formation and preparation for the sacraments, often citing it by paragraph number; shorter local catechisms and the Compendium draw on it.

o: one numbered summary of the faith for the whole Church
a children's question-and-answer book for one country
the rulebook bishops use to run their dioceses

games.q: you're drafting one book of Catholic belief for the whole world. how do you organize it?
o: in four parts: what Catholics believe, celebrate, live and pray.
games.why: four parts: the Creed, the sacraments, life in Christ, and prayer. believe, worship, live, pray.

practice: Of the four parts, believe, worship, live, pray, which one holds a question for you right now, like what is grace, or why confession?
Name that question in a few words and hold it gently, without answering it yet; if you pray, ask for understanding, and if not, just stay curious.
